facts.text: At first they came and went; now the fever is there all the time.
At first they came and went; now my headache keeps getting worse.

facts.item: how long the fevers and headaches have lasted
facts.text: The fevers and headaches started two weeks ago.
I've lost about 10 pounds over the past 9 months.
The left side of my face has gone weak.
I've lost my sense of taste.

facts.item: when the face weakness and the worsening started
facts.text: The face weakness, the loss of taste, the worse headache and the constant fever began about a month after I came back from Mexico.
I've been on adalimumab for my psoriatic arthritis for 6 years.
I stopped it for a while and then started it again.
I've had shingles on my skin before.

findings.name: visual acuity
findings.result: 20/20 in the right eye; 20/50 in the left eye.

findings.name: anterior segment examination
findings.result: Exposure keratopathy of the left eye only; no anterior chamber cell or flare.

findings.name: funduscopic examination
findings.result: Dozens of 100–200 µm, round, creamy yellow-white choroidal infiltrates disseminated throughout both fundi, without vitritis, vasculitis or optic nerve edema.

findings.name: optical coherence tomography
findings.result: Hyporeflective choroidal lesions without macular cysts or thickening.

findings.name: cerebrospinal fluid analysis
findings.result: 8 white blood cells/mm3 (91% lymphocytes); normal glucose and protein.

findings.name: CSF microbiology
findings.result: Cryptococcal antigen negative; negative for other organisms.

findings.name: MRI of the brain and orbits
findings.result: Enhancement of the left facial nerve.

gold.reasoning: 1. Fungal or mycobacterial meningitis — “Given the patient's history of immunosuppressive therapy and travel to Mexico, he was admitted for urgent evaluation for suspected fungal or mycobacterial meningitis… CSF examination was similarly negative for organisms including cryptococcal antigen…” 2. Other infectious etiologies (Lyme, syphilis, tuberculosis, West Nile virus) — “Serum testing for Lyme, syphilis, tuberculosis (TB), and West Nile virus was negative.” 3. Birdshot chorioretinopathy — “Lymphoma and birdshot chorioretinopathy (BSC) are important masquerades for sarcoid-associated choroiditis; however, workup for lymphoma was negative and retinal imaging and examination did not support a diagnosis of BSC.”

source_issues: No vital signs are reported, although fever is a presenting complaint.
The timeline of s001 (two weeks of intermittent symptoms) and s002 (adalimumab interruption, Mexico trip, worsening a month after return) is not fully ordered.
notes: Index visit: the emergency presentation with fevers, worsening headache, left facial weakness and loss of taste (s001-s003); all examinations and tests (s003-s011) belong to that admission workup.

Visual acuity loss in the left eye and the choroidal lesions are not reported as symptoms, so they are findings only; the left facial weakness, which the patient can notice, is both a fact and part of the cranial-nerve finding.
